title: What Makes Things Funny? With Peter McGraw, PhD

sentences.en: A skeleton walks into a bar.
sentences.zh: 有个骷髅走进酒吧。

sentences.en: The bartender says, what do you have?
sentences.zh: 酒保问，你要点点什么？

sentences.en: And the skeleton says, I'll have a beer and a mop.
sentences.zh: 骷髅回答，我要一杯啤酒和一把拖把。

sentences.en: All right, it's an old joke, but maybe you laughed at it.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这是一个老笑话，但也许你听了还是会笑。

sentences.en: And if you did, why?
sentences.zh: 如果你笑了，为什么呢？

sentences.en: What makes it funny?
sentences.zh: 是什么让它变得好笑？

sentences.en: And what is it about puns that tickles our funny bone?
sentences.zh: 双关语到底有什么魔力，能戳中我们的笑点？

sentences.en: Or dad jokes?
sentences.zh: 或者是冷笑话（父亲笑话）？

sentences.en: How about practical jokes?
sentences.zh: 恶作剧怎么样？

sentences.en: Or even a person slipping on a banana peel.
sentences.zh: 甚至是一个人踩到香蕉皮滑倒。

sentences.en: What could possibly tie all of these very different things together under the heading humor?
sentences.zh: 究竟是什么能把这些截然不同的东西，全都归纳到幽默这个标题下呢？

sentences.en: That's a question that's fascinated people for centuries, and not just comedians.
sentences.zh: 这个问题几个世纪以来一直让人着迷，而且不仅仅是喜剧演员。

sentences.en: The writer E.B.
sentences.zh: 作家E.B.

sentences.en: White is supposed to have said that explaining a joke is like dissecting a frog.
sentences.zh: 怀特曾经说过，解释笑话就像解剖青蛙。

sentences.en: The thing dies in the process.
sentences.zh: 在解剖的过程中，青蛙就死掉了。

sentences.en: But scientists and philosophers, undaunted, have nonetheless long tried to figure out what makes some things funny and other things not.
sentences.zh: 但科学家和哲学家们毫不气馁，长期以来一直试图弄清楚，究竟是什么让某些东西好笑，而另一些东西不好笑。

sentences.en: Today, just in time for April Fool's Day, we'll explore that question.
sentences.zh: 今天，正值愚人节之际，我们将探讨这个问题。

sentences.en: And maybe help you figure out whether your practical joke is likely to soar or make people soar at you.
sentences.zh: 也许还能帮你判断，你的恶作剧是会大受欢迎，还是会让人对你白眼相向。

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological Association that examines the links between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学说话》，这是美国心理学会的旗舰播客节目，探讨心理科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯。

sentences.en: Our guest today is Dr. Peter McGraw, a marketing and psychology professor at the University of Colorado Boulder and director of the Humor Research Lab, also known as Hurl.
sentences.zh: 我们今天的嘉宾是彼得·麦格劳博士，他是科罗拉多大学博尔德分校的市场营销与心理学教授，也是幽默研究实验室（简称Hurl）的主任。

sentences.en: He has spent more than a dozen years studying what makes things funny and has developed what he calls the benign violation theory
sentences.zh: 他花了十多年时间研究是什么让事物变得好笑，并提出了他所谓的良性违背理论，

sentences.en: that explains why people find humor in everything from tickling to puns.
sentences.zh: 该理论解释了为什么人们会从胳肢到双关语的各种事物中发现幽默。

sentences.en: He's also explored humor on a more practical level, even trying his hand at stand-up comedy and hosting a podcast where he interviewed comedians about their lives and work.
sentences.zh: 他还从更实用的层面探索了幽默，甚至亲自尝试了单口喜剧，并主持了一个播客，采访喜剧演员的生活和工作。

sentences.en: These days, he's exploring how people can apply lessons from comedy to become more innovative and creative thinkers in all areas of their life and work.
sentences.zh: 如今，他正在探索人们如何将喜剧中的经验教训应用到生活和工作的方方面面，从而成为更具创新性和创造力的思考者。

sentences.en: Thank you for joining us today, Dr. McGraw.
sentences.zh: 感谢你今天做客我们的节目，麦格劳博士。

sentences.en: Kim, it's a great pleasure.
sentences.zh: 金，非常荣幸。

sentences.en: What a wonderful introduction.
sentences.zh: 多么棒的开场白啊。

sentences.en: I actually feel good about myself right now.
sentences.zh: 我现在甚至对自己的感觉挺好。

sentences.en: Well, that's one thing that humor does for us, right?
sentences.zh: 嗯，这就是幽默对我们起到的作用之一，对吧？

sentences.en: It makes us feel pretty good.
sentences.zh: 它让我们感觉相当不错。

sentences.en: Well, let's start by talking about how you got interested in studying the topic.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我们先来谈谈你是如何对研究这个课题产生兴趣的。

sentences.en: What made you as a psychologist want to understand humor?
sentences.zh: 作为一名心理学家，是什么促使你想去理解幽默？

sentences.en: One thing that's probably obvious, like most people, I greatly appreciate good comedy, whether it be consuming it, you know, going to a comedy club or watching a movie.
sentences.zh: 显而易见的一点是，像大多数人一样，我非常欣赏好的喜剧，无论是去消费它，你知道的，去喜剧俱乐部还是看电影。

sentences.en: And then, you know, I would say by professorial standards, I got a kick out of trying to be funny in my professional life, but especially in my personal life.
sentences.zh: 然后，以教授的标准来说，我从在职业生涯中试图表现得有趣中找到了乐趣，在个人生活中更是如此。

sentences.en: And yet, 10 years into my career, at the time I stumbled on this question of what makes things funny, I had never even considered it as a worthy emotional phenomenon to study,
sentences.zh: 然而，在我职业生涯的第十年，当我偶然遇到“究竟是什么让事物变得好笑”这个问题时，我甚至从未把它当作一个值得研究的情感现象来看待，

sentences.en: to research.
sentences.zh: 去进行研究。

sentences.en: And part of it was no one else was doing that.
sentences.zh: 部分原因是没有其他人这样做。

sentences.en: It was, you know, it was running in the background, a little bit of a niche kind of topic, interdisciplinary topic.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，它一直在背景中运行，是一个有点小众的主题，一个跨学科的主题。

sentences.en: One that, as you mentioned, goes back centuries, millennia, to some of the great scholars who psychological science, their ideas were built on.
sentences.zh: 正如你所提到的，这个问题可以追溯到几个世纪、几千年前，追溯到心理科学赖以建立其思想的一些伟大学者。

sentences.en: And I stumbled on this question in a very peculiar way.
sentences.zh: 我以一种非常奇特的方式偶然发现了这个问题。

sentences.en: I was giving a talk at another university about what makes things wrong.
sentences.zh: 当时我在另一所大学做关于“是什么导致事物出错（不道德）”的演讲。

sentences.en: I was studying moral psychology at the time.
sentences.zh: 我当时在研究道德心理学。

sentences.en: And because I want to be a good speaker, I used a kind of provocative, entertaining example of religious marketing that people might find wrong.
sentences.zh: 为了成为一名出色的演讲者，我用了一个具有挑衅性、娱乐性的宗教营销例子，人们可能会觉得这是错误的。

sentences.en: And I got some laughs.
sentences.zh: 我得到了一些笑声。

sentences.en: And a hand went up in the back of the room, and I was asked the most important question of my professional life, actually, maybe the most important question of my life.
sentences.zh: 这时房间后面有一只手举了起来，我被问到了我职业生涯中最重要的问题，实际上，也许是我一生中最重要的问题。

sentences.en: And this professor, she raised her hand, and she just pointed out the incongruity between what I was saying and what was happening,
sentences.zh: 这位女教授举起手，指出了我所说的话和正在发生的事情之间的不一致之处，

sentences.en: which was I was saying that moral violations cause anger and disguSt.
sentences.zh: 那就是我说过，道德违背会导致愤怒和厌恶。

sentences.en: And then she rightfully pointed out, yet we're laughing.
sentences.zh: 然后她理直气壮地指出，然而我们却在笑。

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: And I stood there dumbfounded, and I went back to my university, and I recruited a very bright graduate student, Caleb Warren.
sentences.zh: 我当时站在那里惊呆了，回到大学后，我招募了一位非常聪明的研究生，卡利布·沃伦。

sentences.en: I said, we should answer this question.
sentences.zh: 我说，我们应该回答这个问题。

sentences.en: And, you know, as they say, the rest is history, or at least ongoing history.
sentences.zh: 正如他们所说，剩下的就是历史了，或者至少是正在进行的历史。

sentences.en: Well, then let's dive into the big question that I posed in the introduction, which is, what makes something funny?
sentences.zh: 那么，让我们深入探讨我在引言中提出的那个宏大问题，也就是，究竟是什么让某事变得好笑？

sentences.en: And what is benign violation theory?
sentences.zh: 什么是良性违背理论？

sentences.en: How can it help us answer that question?
sentences.zh: 它如何帮助我们回答这个问题？

sentences.en: So, yeah, so this very bright graduate student, Caleb Warren, and I jumped into a more narrow question, which is, what makes moral violations funny?
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，这位非常聪明的研究生卡利布·沃伦和我深入研究了一个更狭窄的问题，即是什么让道德违背变得好笑？

sentences.en: But in order to answer a question like that, you need a good theory.
sentences.zh: 但为了回答这样的问题，你需要一个好的理论。

sentences.en: So I think the average person doesn't understand what the value of a theory is.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为一般人并不理解理论的价值是什么。

sentences.en: And it's very simple, in my opinion.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，这非常简单。

sentences.en: A good theory helps you answer questions.
sentences.zh: 一个好的理论可以帮你回答问题。

sentences.en: And so it doesn't have to be totally right.
sentences.zh: 所以它不必完全正确。

sentences.en: It just has to be good enough.
sentences.zh: 它只需要足够好就行。

sentences.en: And then a good theory will allow you then to make predictions about questions you haven't even considered yet.
sentences.zh: 然后，一个好的理论能让你对那些你甚至还没有考虑过的问题做出预测。

sentences.en: And so we got started on this, and our look at the literature was disappointing.
sentences.zh: 于是我们开始了这项研究，但我们查阅文献的结果令人失望。

sentences.en: So I did something I'm not proud of, Kim.
sentences.zh: 所以我做了一件我并不引以为豪的事，金。

sentences.en: I Googled what makes things funny.
sentences.zh: 我用谷歌搜索了“是什么让事物变得好笑”。

sentences.en: That was my starting point.
sentences.zh: 那是我的起点。

sentences.en: That's what my undergraduates do when I give them an assignment, you know, like they just Google this.
sentences.zh: 当我给本科生布置作业时，他们也会这么做，你知道的，他们就会去谷歌上搜一下。

sentences.en: And what I found was hearkening all the way back to these Greek philosophers, Aristotle, Plato, and then other great thinkers, Immanuel Kant, Thomas Hobbes, Sigmund Freud, frankly,
sentences.zh: 我发现，一直追溯到这些希腊哲学家亚里士多德、柏拉图，以及后来的其他伟大思想家，伊曼纽尔·康德、托马斯·霍布斯、西格蒙德·弗洛伊德，坦白说，

sentences.en: people way, way smarter than me, had put forth theories of humor.
sentences.zh: 那些比我聪明得多的人，都曾提出过关于幽默的理论。

sentences.en: And those theories take one of three flavors.
sentences.zh: 这些理论大致可以分为三种风格。

sentences.en: They point out what we call superiority theory.
sentences.zh: 他们提出了我们所说的优越感理论。

sentences.en: We laugh at something that we sort of laugh at the follies and foibles of others.
sentences.zh: 我们嘲笑某些事物，有点像在嘲笑别人的愚蠢和怪癖。

sentences.en: Relief theory or release theory, which is humor is this kind of release of tension that we carry around all the time.
sentences.zh: 宣泄理论或释放理论，即幽默是我们随身携带的一种紧张感的释放。

sentences.en: Freud's responsible largely for that.
sentences.zh: 弗洛伊德对此负有很大责任。

sentences.en: And then the 800-pound gorilla of humor theories, incongruity theory.
sentences.zh: 然后是幽默理论中的庞然大物，不一致性理论。

sentences.en: We laugh at some mismatch there.
sentences.zh: 我们为某种错位而笑。

sentences.en: And what we realized, I think, very quickly, and the benefit of coming to it as I was approaching mid-career, was it just, first of all,
sentences.zh: 我想我们很快就意识到，而且以我接近职业生涯中期的视角来看，首先，

sentences.en: it didn't make sense that we need three theories of humor.
sentences.zh: 我们需要三个幽默理论，这在逻辑上说不通。

sentences.en: That a good theory is what we call parsimonious, right?
sentences.zh: 一个好的理论应该是我们所说的简约的，对吧？

sentences.en: It's simple.
sentences.zh: 它是简单的。

sentences.en: And that you don't, you shouldn't have to select from a menu.
sentences.zh: 你不应该非得从菜单中进行选择。

sentences.en: Like, well, this theory works for pratfalls, but that theory works for puns.
sentences.zh: 比如，这个理论适用于滑稽跌倒，但那个理论适用于双关语。

sentences.en: And so we found this sort of little known paper written by a linguist that served as the basis for, as you called it, the benign violation theory.
sentences.zh: 于是我们发现了这篇鲜为人知的由语言学家撰写的论文，它成为了你所谓的“良性违背理论”的基础。

sentences.en: And in short, what we found was, and we find time and time again in Hurl, is that people laugh at, they're amused by,
sentences.zh: 简而言之，我们所发现的，并且在Hurl实验室中一次又一次发现的是，人们会因为以下原因而发笑、感到被逗乐、

sentences.en: they judge something as funny if it is simultaneously wrong yet okay, threatening yet safe, doesn't make sense yet makes sense.
sentences.zh: 并将某事评判为好笑：当它同时既是错误又没问题、既具有威胁又安全、既讲不通又讲得通时。

sentences.en: So you can imagine kind of a Venn diagram, an overlap between benign and violation.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以想象一个韦恩图，即良性和违背之间的重叠。

sentences.en: And what happens is the violation gives us arousal, makes us concerned, and then what we call the benign appraisal, seeing how this is okay, flips it and turns it from bad to good.
sentences.zh: 发生的情况是，违背带给我们唤醒，让我们感到担忧，然后我们所说的良性评估——看到这其实没问题——将其反转，化坏为好。

sentences.en: And we laugh to tell the world this thing that seems so threatening is actually harmless.
sentences.zh: 我们发笑是为了向世界宣告，这个看起来如此具有威胁性的东西其实是无害的。

sentences.en: Before I forget, what was that moral juxtaposition that made people laugh?
sentences.zh: 在我忘记之前，那个让人发笑的道德并置是什么？

sentences.en: So in this research, I was looking at how some people find religious marketing to be morally reprehensible, for churches to use commercial principles to save souls.
sentences.zh: 在这项研究中，我观察了为什么有些人会认为宗教营销是道德上应受谴责的，因为教堂为了拯救灵魂而使用商业原则。

sentences.en: And they just find it icky.
sentences.zh: 他们只是觉得这很恶心。

sentences.en: And they're concerned that it may take you away from the righteousness that religion may have.
sentences.zh: 他们担心这可能会让你背离宗教可能拥有的正义感。

sentences.en: The example was a church in Tampa, Florida, that had very good intentions.
sentences.zh: 这个例子是佛罗里达州坦帕市的一家教堂，他们有着非常好的意图。

sentences.en: And that was to get people to go to its winter retreat.
sentences.zh: 那就是吸引人们去参加它的冬季静修。

sentences.en: You want to save souls?
sentences.zh: 你想拯救灵魂吗？

sentences.en: Let's get people to the winter retreat.
sentences.zh: 让我们把人们吸引到冬季静修来。

sentences.en: And so they decided to have a raffle.
sentences.zh: 于是他们决定举办一次抽奖活动。

sentences.en: So come to the winter retreat, you get enrolled in the raffle.
sentences.zh: 所以来参加冬季静修，你就能报名参加抽奖。

sentences.en: And what people found funny was the choice of grand prize.
sentences.zh: 而人们觉得好笑的是特等奖的选择。

sentences.en: And that was a yellow H2 Hummer SUV.
sentences.zh: 那就是一辆黄色的悍马H2越野车。

sentences.en: So not exactly a gut buster, but good for a chuckle.
sentences.zh: 所以虽然算不上让人捧腹大笑，但也足以让人轻笑一声。

sentences.en: Take it on the road to paradise.
sentences.zh: 开着它驶向天堂之路。

sentences.en: And what we found to be the case was, depending on your perspective about how wrong or right that was, that example was funny or not.
sentences.zh: 我们发现的情况是，取决于你对这件事是对是错的看法，这个例子究竟好不好笑因人而异。

sentences.en: And so those academics who aren't very religious, don't have a very strong connection to this church and so on,
sentences.zh: 因此，那些不太宗教、与这个教堂没有太强联系的学者们等等，

sentences.en: they were able to see how it was both wrong and funny at the same time.
sentences.zh: 他们能够看出这件事怎么会既是错误的又同时是好笑的。

sentences.en: So how do you study humor in a lab?
sentences.zh: 那么你如何在实验室里研究幽默呢？

sentences.en: What are the experiments that you've done over?
sentences.zh: 你做过哪些实验？

sentences.en: I mean, I'm sure you can't tell us all of them,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我确信你不能把所有的实验都告诉我们，

sentences.en: but maybe a couple that you've done over the years that have helped you formulate the theory and better understand what makes things funny.
sentences.zh: 但也许可以分享一两个你这些年来做过的实验，它们帮助你构建了理论，并更好地理解了是什么让事物变得好笑。

sentences.en: So I'll give you an example of one of, I think, one of the more fun ones.
sentences.zh: 那我给你们举一个其中比较有趣的例子。

sentences.en: So a lot of them, I admit, is just basically showing people funny images or funny jokes and then just asking them, how amusing is this?
sentences.zh: 所以我承认，很多实验基本上就是向人们展示有趣的图片或好笑的笑话，然后直接问他们，这有多好笑？

sentences.en: Did you laugh?
sentences.zh: 你笑了吗？

sentences.en: Do you find this offensive?
sentences.zh: 你觉得这冒犯人吗？

sentences.en: Do you find it boring?
sentences.zh: 你觉得这无聊吗？

sentences.en: And by the way, this is an important set of questions.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，这是一套很重要的问题。

sentences.en: Because in any study we do that we ask someone a judgment, we ask three styles of questions.
sentences.zh: 因为在我们进行的任何要求某人做出评判的研究中，我们都会问三种风格的问题。

sentences.en: One is, how amused are you, right?
sentences.zh: 一个是，你有多开心（被逗乐），对吧？

sentences.en: Getting at that experience of humor.
sentences.zh: 探究那种幽默的体验。

sentences.en: We ask, are you offended?
sentences.zh: 我们问，你被冒犯了吗？

sentences.en: And if so, by how much?
sentences.zh: 如果是的话，程度有多深？

sentences.en: And are you bored?
sentences.zh: 以及你觉得无聊吗？

sentences.en: And if so, by how much?
sentences.zh: 如果是的话，程度有多深？

sentences.en: And the reason for that is a joke can fail in two different ways.
sentences.zh: 这样做的原因是一个笑话可能会以两种不同的方式失败。

sentences.en: You mentioned dad jokes.
sentences.zh: 你提到了冷笑话（父亲笑话）。

sentences.en: Dad jokes, when they're not funny, are rarely ever offensive.
sentences.zh: 冷笑话在不好笑的时候，几乎从来都不是冒犯性的。

sentences.en: They fall on the boring side of the continuum.
sentences.zh: 它们落在连续统的无聊那一侧。

sentences.en: But there's a lot of jokes that are very risque.
sentences.zh: 但有很多笑话是非常低俗的。

sentences.en: And when those jokes fail, people are offended.
sentences.zh: 当这些笑话失败时，人们会感到被冒犯。

sentences.en: They're outraged.
sentences.zh: 他们会感到愤怒。

sentences.en: And so a good theory of humor is able to not only predict when something's going to be funny, but also when it fails to be funny, which side does it fall on?
sentences.zh: 因此，一个好的幽默理论不仅能够预测某事何时会好笑，还能预测当它未能变得好笑时，它会落在哪一侧？

sentences.en: And so we always ask those questions.
sentences.zh: 所以我们总是会问这些问题。

sentences.en: But this one was designed to measure smiling and laughter.
sentences.zh: 但这个实验旨在衡量微笑和大笑。

sentences.en: And I'll give you an example from it.
sentences.zh: 我给你们举个其中的例子。

sentences.en: We've always been very critical of incongruity theory because one is oftentimes incongruity is not well defined.
sentences.zh: 我们一直对不一致性理论持高度批判态度，因为一方面，不一致性往往没有得到很好的定义。

sentences.en: But oftentimes what people will say is, and if you ask the regular everyday person what makes something funny, they'll say something surprising.
sentences.zh: 但人们经常会说，如果你问普通人是什么让某事变得好笑，他们会说出人意料的东西。

sentences.en: We laugh at things that are surprising.
sentences.zh: 我们嘲笑那些出人意料的事物。

sentences.en: And we make the argument that actually that's neither necessary nor sufficient for humor.
sentences.zh: 而我们的观点是，实际上这既不是幽默的必要条件，也不是充分条件。

sentences.en: For example, we laugh at jokes that we know the punchline to.
sentences.zh: 例如，我们会嘲笑那些我们已经知道包袱（笑点）的笑话。

sentences.en: That is, there's nothing surprising about them.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，它们没有什么出人意料的地方。

sentences.en: I rewatched There's Something About Mary, you know, 20, 30 years after it came out.
sentences.zh: 我重看了《我为玛丽狂》，你知道的，是在它上映20、30年之后。

sentences.en: By the way, still very funny.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，依然非常搞笑。

sentences.en: And I know all the jokes.
sentences.zh: 而且我知道所有的笑话。

sentences.en: And I found myself laughing.
sentences.zh: 结果我发现自己还是笑个不停。

sentences.en: So in this study, we had our subjects engaged in a conversation with what we call a confederate, basically a research assistant who's posing as a student.
sentences.zh: 所以在这次研究中，我们让受试者与我们所谓的同谋进行对话，基本上就是一个伪装成学生的助理研究员。

sentences.en: This is a very common technique in psychological studies.
sentences.zh: 这是心理学研究中非常常见的一种技术。

sentences.en: And we basically at some point in the interaction, the person grabbed a handful of Skittles and threw them at the subject.
sentences.zh: 我们基本上在互动的某个时刻，这个人抓了一把彩虹糖（Skittles）向受试者扔去。

sentences.en: Which might seem to be kind of an insulting thing to do.
sentences.zh: 这看起来可能是一种有点侮辱性的行为。

sentences.en: In one of the conditions, though, we either announced, I'm going to throw these Skittles at you.
sentences.zh: 然而，在其中一个实验条件中，我们提前宣布了：“我要把这些彩虹糖扔向你。”

sentences.en: Or I'm not, you know, or didn't say they were going to throw the Skittles at them.
sentences.zh: 或者说我没有，你知道的，或者没说他们打算把彩虹糖砸向他们。

sentences.en: And in that condition where they announced it and threw the Skittles, there was actually more laughter than when not.
sentences.zh: 而且在他们宣布并扔彩虹糖的那种情况下，实际上的笑声比不扔的时候更多。

sentences.en: In part because, and we did this to show that surprise is not necessary for comedy.
sentences.zh: 部分原因在于，我们做这个是为了证明喜剧并不一定需要意外。

sentences.en: Right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: You know what I mean?
sentences.zh: 你知道我的意思吗？

sentences.en: But the less surprising condition in that experiment was actually got more smiles and laughter than the surprising condition.
sentences.zh: 但那个实验中不够意外的那种情况，实际上比意外的情况获得了更多的微笑和笑声。

sentences.en: So there's a saying that humor is tragedy plus time.
sentences.zh: 所以有这样一句名言：幽默等于悲剧加上时间。

sentences.en: And you've written about when it's too soon to joke about something tragic.
sentences.zh: 而你写过关于什么时候拿悲剧开玩笑还为时尚早的文章。

sentences.en: What is the answer?
sentences.zh: 答案是什么？

sentences.en: How long does it take?
sentences.zh: 需要多长时间？

sentences.en: And can you say before we can find humor in tragedy?
sentences.zh: 在你看来，在我们能在悲剧里找到幽默之前能确定时间吗？

sentences.en: I'm glad you asked that question because we ran a huge cross-sectional study to answer that very question.
sentences.zh: 很高兴你问了这个问题，因为我们做了一项大型的横断面研究来回答这个问题。

sentences.en: I'm going to give away the punchline before I describe the study.
sentences.zh: 在我描述这项研究之前，我要先剧透一下。

sentences.en: And the answer is the amount of time depends on a lot of things, including how big a violation it is.
sentences.zh: 答案是，时间的长短取决于很多事情，包括违背常规的程度有多大。

sentences.en: But we, as a result of that work, we revised the idea that comedy is tragedy plus time to be comedy is tragedy plus the right amount of time.
sentences.zh: 但由于这项工作，我们修正了喜剧是悲剧加上时间的观点，将其改为喜剧是悲剧加上恰当的时间。

sentences.en: And I'll lead with an intuition, and that is there's lots of things that are too soon, and then at some point it becomes okay to joke about them.
sentences.zh: 我先凭直觉说一点，那就是有很多事情在当时都为时尚早，然后在某个时刻拿它们开玩笑就变得可以接受了。

sentences.en: But at some point enough time passes that that thing is no longer worthy of being joked about.
sentences.zh: 但在某个时刻，足够的时间流逝之后，那件事就不再值得拿来开玩笑了。

sentences.en: And so what you get is too soon has the outrage, too late is boring.
sentences.zh: 所以你会发现，为时尚早会引起愤怒，太迟了则会令人厌烦。

sentences.en: And there's, again, that sweet spot, that peak in terms of time.
sentences.zh: 而且，再次说明，存在那个黄金点，也就是时间上的那个峰值。

sentences.en: Why is it the time helps make something funnier?
sentences.zh: 为什么时间有助于让某事变得更有趣？

sentences.en: Well, because the passage of time creates distance from it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，因为时间的流逝创造了距离感。

sentences.en: And distance, whether it be the passage of time or physical distance or relational distance, helps turn violations into benign violations by removing their threat.
sentences.zh: 而距离感，无论是时间的流逝、物理距离还是关系距离，都可以通过消除威胁，将违背转变为良性违背。

sentences.en: And so in that study, what we did was we measured people's reactions to a parody account of Hurricane Katrina.
sentences.zh: 所以在那个研究中，我们做的是衡量人们对一个模仿卡特里娜飓风的账号的反应。

sentences.en: And what we found was, as Katrina was wreaking havoc on the New York metropolitan area, the jokes coming out of this parody account weren't funny.
sentences.zh: 我们发现，当卡特里娜飓风在纽约大都会区肆虐时，这个模仿账号发出的笑话一点也不好笑。

sentences.en: Then, with the passage of time, they started to become funny and less offensive.
sentences.zh: 然后，随着时间的推移，它们开始变得好笑，也没那么冒犯了。

sentences.en: And then further, months and months later, those jokes no longer seemed relevant.
sentences.zh: 再往后，几个月又几个月过去，那些笑话似乎就不再相关了。

sentences.en: They were boring.
sentences.zh: 它们变得索然无味。

sentences.en: And so I can't remember the exact date, but it was like 39 days after Hurricane Katrina, we found that those jokes peaked.
sentences.zh: 我不记得确切日期了，但大概是在卡特里娜飓风过后39天，我们发现那些笑话达到了笑点的顶峰。

sentences.en: Now, of course, in some cases, it peaks an hour later.
sentences.zh: 当然，在某些情况下，一个小时后就达到顶峰了。

sentences.en: In some cases, it peaks.
sentences.zh: 在某些情况下，它会达到顶峰。

sentences.en: And there are some tragedies in the world that may never peak, because it never becomes okay to joke.
sentences.zh: 世界上有些悲剧可能永远不会达到顶峰，因为开玩笑永远不会变得可以接受。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: That was my next question, which is, are there some topics that are just never funny?
sentences.zh: 这是我的下一个问题，那就是，有没有某些话题是永远都不会好笑的？

sentences.en: Well, you know, I think it depends on who you talk to.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道的，我认为这取决于你跟谁谈论。

sentences.en: I think a comic says, there's no such thing as too soon if a joke is funny.
sentences.zh: 我认为喜剧演员会说，如果一个笑话好笑，就没有什么为时尚早一说。

sentences.en: I, you know, I know, I have Israeli friends who make Holocaust jokes.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我知道，我有犹太朋友会拿大屠杀开玩笑。

sentences.en: They have some sort of license that non-Jewish people don't have.
sentences.zh: 他们拥有某种非犹太人不具备的特权。

sentences.en: And so what that question reveals is the incredible complexity around studying humor is part of the reason that people haven't studied it,
sentences.zh: 所以这个问题揭示了围绕幽默研究的难以置信的复杂性，这也是人们一直没有对其进行研究的部分原因，

sentences.en: because at first blush, it seems so mysterious.
sentences.zh: 因为乍一看，它显得如此神秘。

sentences.en: It seems so difficult.
sentences.zh: 它看起来如此困难。

sentences.en: But as you know, as someone who values science,
sentences.zh: 但正如你所知，作为一个珍视科学的人，

sentences.en: science has the ability to take the complex and explain it.
sentences.zh: 科学有能力将复杂的事物剥丝抽茧并加以解释。

sentences.en: If we can map the human genome, you know, we can figure out what makes things funny.
sentences.zh: 如果我们能绘制人类基因组图谱，你知道的，我们就能弄清楚是什么让事物变得好笑。

sentences.en: We just need to have an experiment.
sentences.zh: 我们只需要做一个实验。

sentences.en: How much does what's considered funny vary by country or culture?
sentences.zh: 被认为好笑的事物因国家或文化而异的程度有多大？

sentences.en: Are there universal jokes or universal type humor?
sentences.zh: 是否存在普遍的笑话或普遍类型的幽默？

sentences.en: So there's very little that's universal when it comes to comedy, to be honeSt.
sentences.zh: 老实说，在喜剧方面，真正普遍的东西微乎其微。

sentences.en: But the explanation for this is, as I said, a good theory explains puzzles.
sentences.zh: 但对这一现象的解释是，正如我所说，一个好的理论能够解释谜题。

sentences.en: And one of the puzzles is, why are there two ways that a joke can fail?
sentences.zh: 其中一个谜题是，为什么笑话会以两种方式失效？

sentences.en: Which we've already alluded to.
sentences.zh: 我们之前已经暗示过这一点。

sentences.en: It could be too benign or it could be too much of a violation.
sentences.zh: 它可能过于温和无害，也可能违背得太过火。

sentences.en: But also, how can the same joke make one person laugh, another person yawn, and another person stomp their feet with outrage?
sentences.zh: 但同时，同一个笑话怎么能让一个人大笑，另一个人打哈欠，还有一个人气得直跺脚呢？

sentences.en: And at least from a theoretical standpoint, we can explain this.
sentences.zh: 至少从理论的角度来看，我们可以解释这一点。

sentences.en: And that is, what is wrong and what is okay?
sentences.zh: 那就是，什么是错的，什么是可以接受的？

sentences.en: What is benign and what is a violation?
sentences.zh: 什么是无害的，什么是违背常规的？

sentences.en: Depends on the individual, the audience members, values, beliefs, lifestyle, the number of drinks they've had, the context they're in, right?
sentences.zh: 这取决于个人、观众的价值观、信仰、生活方式、他们喝了多少酒、他们所处的环境，对吧？

sentences.en: Whether they're in a comedy club or in a church.
sentences.zh: 无论是身处喜剧俱乐部还是教堂。

sentences.en: And of course, their culture.
sentences.zh: 当然，还有他们的文化。

sentences.en: Because culture creates norMs.
sentences.zh: 因为文化创造了规范。

sentences.en: Culture creates rules.
sentences.zh: 文化创造了规则。

sentences.en: And a lot of comedy breaks rules.
sentences.zh: 而很多喜剧都在打破规则。

sentences.en: And so it depends on what rules you value and don't value in that way.
sentences.zh: 所以这取决于你在那种情况下珍视哪些规则、不珍视哪些规则。

sentences.en: Now, what is likely to be universal?
sentences.zh: 那么，什么东西最可能是普遍存在的呢？

sentences.en: The most universal thing is physical comedy.
sentences.zh: 最普遍的东西是肢体喜剧。

sentences.en: That is, on the individual level, things like tickling and play fighting.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，在个体层面，诸如挠痒痒和假装打斗之类的事情。

sentences.en: And we know this because non-human primates laugh when play fighting.
sentences.zh: 我们之所以知道这一点，是因为非人类灵长类动物在假装打斗时也会笑。

sentences.en: Even, and this is mind-blowing, Kim, you can type into YouTube, rat laughter, and you will find videos of rats being tickled and them doing the rat equivalent of laughing.
sentences.zh: 甚至——这太让人匪夷所思了，金——你可以在YouTube上输入“老鼠笑声”，你会发现有视频记录老鼠被挠痒痒，它们发出了相当于老鼠的笑声。

sentences.en: Now, when you take this into the world of comedy, the closest we can come to is the classic, as you mentioned on the intro, slipping on a banana peel, right?
sentences.zh: 现在，当你把这个带入喜剧世界时，我们能想到的最接近的例子就是经典桥段，正如你在开场时提到的，踩到香蕉皮滑倒，对吧？

sentences.en: And the reason behind that is when someone falls, falls down a flight of stairs or something like that, that is obviously a violation.
sentences.zh: 背后的原因在于，当某人摔倒、从一连串楼梯上摔下来或类似情况时，这显然是一种违背（安全）的状况。

sentences.en: We're concerned for their safety.
sentences.zh: 我们为他们的安全感到担忧。

sentences.en: But if there's something about that that makes it safe, perhaps they get up and find, dust themselves off, and look perplexed.
sentences.zh: 但如果其中有什么因素让它变得安全，也许他们站起来，拍拍身上的灰尘，露出了困惑的表情。

sentences.en: Maybe there's someone we want to fall down a flight of stairs, right?
sentences.zh: 也许有那么一个人，我们就是想看他从楼梯上摔下去，对吧？

sentences.en: You know what I mean?
sentences.zh: 你知道我的意思吗？

sentences.en: And so there's these different ways.
sentences.zh: 所以有这些不同的方式。

sentences.en: Now, that's as close as we come because there are no cultural norMs.
sentences.zh: 现在，这是我们能做到的最接近的程度了，因为不存在文化规范。

sentences.en: There is no language.
sentences.zh: 这里没有语言。

sentences.en: And it all is connected to that idea of physical play.
sentences.zh: 这一切都与那种肢体游戏的理念息息相关。

sentences.en: But as you know, not everybody finds pratfalls to be amusing.
sentences.zh: 但如你所知，并不是每个人都觉得滑稽跌倒很有趣。

sentences.en: And so there are real limits to the universality of comedy.
sentences.zh: 因此，喜剧的普遍性是存在真正的局限性的。

sentences.en: And pratfalls also, it's, if you know the person who fell or had the pratfall is funnier, right,
sentences.zh: 而且滑稽跌倒还有一点，如果你认识那个摔倒或出丑的人，会更好笑，对吧，

sentences.en: than if it's a total stranger where you don't know whether that person got hurt or what might have happened.
sentences.zh: 总好过那是一个完全的陌生人，你根本不知道那个人有没有受伤或者发生了什么。

sentences.en: Yeah, it depends.
sentences.zh: 是的，这得看情况。

sentences.en: I mean, look, I love it when my friends fall up a flight of stairs, but I don't like it when my friends fall down a flight of stairs.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，听着，我喜欢看我的朋友往上走楼梯时绊倒，但我不喜欢看我的朋友从楼梯上摔下来。

sentences.en: So is a sense of humor correlated with higher intelligence?
sentences.zh: 那么幽默感与更高的智商相关吗？

sentences.en: It just seems to me that smart people get jokes and people who are maybe not quite as intelligent.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，聪明人能懂笑话，而那些可能没那么聪明的人……

sentences.en: Now, I'm not even sure how I'm defining that.
sentences.zh: 现在，我甚至不确定我该如何定义这一点。

sentences.en: That's wide open.
sentences.zh: 这完全是个开放的问题。

sentences.en: But can you be – and my other question that's related to this is can you be intelligent and have no sense of humor?
sentences.zh: 但你能不能——我另一个与之相关的问题是，你能不能既聪明又完全没有幽默感？

sentences.en: Yes and yes.
sentences.zh: 可以，完全可以。

sentences.en: So, first of all, we should be – when people talk about a sense of humor, we should be clear.
sentences.zh: 所以，首先，当人们谈论幽默感时，我们应该搞清楚。

sentences.en: There's two sides of a sense of humor, and they're surprisingly uncorrelated.
sentences.zh: 幽默感有两个方面，而它们出人意料地并不相关。

sentences.en: That is, your ability to produce laughter in others and the likelihood that you laugh in response to someone's attempt to produce laughter in others.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，你逗笑别人的能力，与你在别人试图逗笑你时笑出声的可能性。

sentences.en: And the little work that's been done finds that those things are surprisingly uncorrelated,
sentences.zh: 已经做过的一些微薄研究发现，这两者出人意料地不相关，

sentences.en: that someone who might be very good at making people laugh may not be very easy to laugh and vice versa.
sentences.zh: 一个非常擅长把别人逗笑的人，自己可能并不容易笑出来，反之亦然。

sentences.en: However, when it comes to the production of comedy, you are correct.
sentences.zh: 然而，当谈到喜剧创作时，你是对的。

sentences.en: Your intuition is absolutely correct.
sentences.zh: 你的直觉绝对是正确的。

sentences.en: Smart people are better than less smart people.
sentences.zh: 聪明人比不太聪明的人做得更好。

sentences.en: And that makes sense, I think.
sentences.zh: 我想这说得通。

sentences.en: One is intelligence is correlated with creativity.
sentences.zh: 其一是智商与创造力息息相关。

sentences.en: And creativity really is at the foundation of this process.
sentences.zh: 而创造力确实是这个过程的基石。

sentences.en: Smart people are knowledgeable about the world.
sentences.zh: 聪明人对这个世界了解很多。

sentences.en: And so, if you want to be able to make comedy, a lot of comedy is about what's happening in the world, you know, in that sense.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你想创作喜剧，很多喜剧都与世界上正在发生的事情有关，你知道的，从这个意义上说。

sentences.en: And then lastly, it really is, and this is not something we've talked about to this point, but there is a third element to the benign violation theory.
sentences.zh: 最后，确实如此——这也是我们之前没有讨论过的一点——良性违背理论还有一个第三要素。

sentences.en: And that is that judgment of wrong and okay has to occur simultaneously.
sentences.zh: 那就是对错误和可以接受的判断必须同时发生。

sentences.en: And so, that term being quick-witted really is about how do you bring those appraisals together at the same time.
sentences.zh: 所以，“机智”这个词实际上是指你如何同时做出这两种评估。

sentences.en: And that's not easy to do.
sentences.zh: 要做到这一点可不容易。

sentences.en: We know that most humor attempts fail.
sentences.zh: 我们知道大多数幽默尝试都以失败告终。

sentences.en: We know that most professionals really have to write lots and lots of jokes in order to find that one very, very good joke.
sentences.zh: 我们知道大多数专业人士为了找到那一个非常非常好的笑话，真的必须写大量大量的笑话。

sentences.en: And so, being smart certainly helps.
sentences.zh: 所以，聪明肯定是有帮助的。

sentences.en: Now, I want to be clear, being smart is not in the traditional sense of getting high GREs or high SATs necessarily.
sentences.zh: 现在，我想明确一点，这里的聪明并不一定是指传统意义上考取很高的GRE或SAT分数。

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 确实。

sentences.en: Because, you know, we often have that class clown who is very, very good at making people laugh,
sentences.zh: 因为，你知道的，我们经常有那种班级里的调皮鬼，非常非常擅长把别人逗笑，

sentences.en: may not actually excel in traditional forms of education, in part because they're counter-normative.
sentences.zh: 可能在传统形式的教育中并不拔尖，部分原因在于他们反常规。

sentences.en: They don't behave.
sentences.zh: 他们不守规矩。

sentences.en: And so on.
sentences.zh: 诸如此类。

sentences.en: So, really, it's not about the, the, valedictorians I actually don't think are the funniest people.
sentences.zh: 所以，实际上，这并不是关于……我其实觉得那些成绩名列前茅的优秀毕业生并不是最搞笑的人。

sentences.en: Right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: It's the people who are smart but also can sit in this space where they're willing to break some rules.
sentences.zh: 是那些既聪明又能处于这种愿意打破一些常规的空间里的人。

sentences.en: Valedictorians are very good at following rules.
sentences.zh: 优秀毕业生非常擅长遵守规则。

sentences.en: They're not very good at breaking rules.
sentences.zh: 他们不太擅长打破规则。

sentences.en: It's sort of more the entrepreneurial person, I think, who has that, that edge.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这更像是那种具有创业精神、自带锋芒的人。

sentences.en: You published a paper a little while ago on humorous complaining and found that if you have something you want to gripe about,
sentences.zh: 不久前你发表了一篇关于幽默抱怨的论文，发现如果你有什么想抱怨的事情，

sentences.en: that there are advantages and disadvantages to complaining in a funny way.
sentences.zh: 以幽默的方式抱怨既有优点也有缺点。

sentences.en: Can you talk about that a little bit?
sentences.zh: 你能稍微谈谈那个吗？

sentences.en: What'd you find?
sentences.zh: 你发现了什么？

sentences.en: I'd be happy to.
sentences.zh: 我很乐意。

sentences.en: That, I have to say that, that might be my favorite paper.
sentences.zh: 我必须说，那可能是我最喜欢的一篇论文。

sentences.en: And I came to the idea behind that paper through, I caught myself claiming that I don't complain about things.
sentences.zh: 我萌生那篇论文的想法是因为，我发现自己声称我从不抱怨事情。

sentences.en: Which is completely false.
sentences.zh: 而这完全是假话。

sentences.en: It's not even, I complain all the time.
sentences.zh: 甚至都不是，我无时无刻不在抱怨。

sentences.en: You know why?
sentences.zh: 你知道为什么吗？

sentences.en: Because humans complain all the time.
sentences.zh: 因为人类无时无刻不在抱怨。

sentences.en: People complain all the time.
sentences.zh: 人们无时无刻不在抱怨。

sentences.en: Because complaining, in some ways, is useful and sometimes falsely useful.
sentences.zh: 因为抱怨在某些方面是有用的，有时甚至是虚假的有用。

sentences.en: That is, we have theories about the value of complaining.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，我们对抱怨的价值有一些理论。

sentences.en: Not all of them are correct.
sentences.zh: 并非所有这些理论都是正确的。

sentences.en: So, for example, complaining actually doesn't help us through catharsis in the way that we think it does.
sentences.zh: 举个例子，抱怨实际上并没有像我们想象的那样通过宣泄来帮助我们度过难关。

sentences.en: It does help us because suppressing a complaint is really bad.
sentences.zh: 它确实对我们有帮助，因为压抑抱怨真的很糟糕。

sentences.en: Suppressing an emotion tends to make it worse.
sentences.zh: 压抑情绪往往会让情况变得更糟。

sentences.en: But sometimes people complain in order to get, to get something.
sentences.zh: 但有时人们抱怨是为了达到某种目的，为了得到某些东西。

sentences.en: Sometimes they complain to show the world that they have expertise.
sentences.zh: 有时他们抱怨是为了向世界展示他们拥有专业知识。

sentences.en: So, I complain, oh, this dessert, oh, it's terrible.
sentences.zh: 所以，我抱怨，噢，这道甜点，噢，太糟糕了。

sentences.en: Because I want the world to know, I know what good food tastes like.
sentences.zh: 因为我想让全世界知道，我知道真正的好食物是什么味道。

sentences.en: And so on.
sentences.zh: 诸如此类。

sentences.en: But what I found was, I am a complainer.
sentences.zh: 但我发现的是，我是一个爱抱怨的人。

sentences.en: But I tend to be a humorous complainer.
sentences.zh: 但我往往是一个以幽默方式抱怨的人。

sentences.en: I make a lot of, like, sarcastic and weedy quips to make people laugh about the bad weather, the bad traffic, you know, a bad dessert, and so on and so forth.
sentences.zh: 我会开很多诸如此类的讽刺和刻薄的玩笑，来让大家拿糟糕的天气、糟糕的交通、你知道的，糟糕的甜点等等事情开玩笑。

sentences.en: And so, this makes sense, right?
sentences.zh: 所以，这说得通，对吧？

sentences.en: A complaint is an expression of something negative.
sentences.zh: 抱怨是对负面事物的一种表达。

sentences.en: And a joke is a way to take something negative and make it positive.
sentences.zh: 而笑话则是将消极事物转化为积极事物的一种方式。

sentences.en: And so, this work on humorous complaining, Caleb Warren was a co-author on that paper also, what we found was people like humorous complainers,
sentences.zh: 而且，关于幽默抱怨这项研究，卡勒布·沃伦（Caleb Warren）也是那篇论文的合著者，我们发现人们喜欢幽默的抱怨者，

sentences.en: humorous complaints are attention-getting, people will share humorous complaints.
sentences.zh: 幽默的抱怨很吸引眼球，人们会分享幽默的抱怨。

sentences.en: So, if you want to complain about a company, a humorous complaint is great if you want it to, quote, unquote, go viral.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你想对一家公司进行抱怨，如果你想让它，也就是所谓的，引发病毒式传播，那么幽默的抱怨是非常棒的。

sentences.en: The downside of humorous complaints are they don't spur the kind of reaction we often want them to.
sentences.zh: 幽默抱怨的缺点在于，它们不会激起我们通常希望它们引发的那种反应。

sentences.en: If you complain to your roommate about the dishes in the sink, that may get him or her to clean the dishes.
sentences.zh: 如果你向室友抱怨水槽里的碗，这可能会促使他或她去洗碗。

sentences.en: But if you make humorous complaints about the dishes in the sink, you're taking this thing that's wrong and making it okay.
sentences.zh: 但如果你对水槽里的碗进行幽默的抱怨，你就是在把这件错误的事情变得可以接受。

sentences.en: And so, as a result, it may not spur the kind of remedial behavior that you want in that sense.
sentences.zh: 因此，从某种意义上说，它可能无法激起你所希望的那种纠正行为。

sentences.en: And so, what I say is, you know, pick your weapon depending on which of the outcomes that you want for a complaint.
sentences.zh: 所以，我的建议是，你知道的，根据你对抱怨所期望的结果来选择你的武器。

sentences.en: What is the relationship and the difference, say, between laughter and humor?
sentences.zh: 比如说，笑声和幽默之间的关系和区别是什么？

sentences.en: We laugh at funny things, but there's nervous laughter, there's uncomfortable laughter.
sentences.zh: 我们会因为好笑的事情而笑，但也有紧张的笑，有尴尬的笑。

sentences.en: So, how are laughter and humor related?
sentences.zh: 那么，笑声和幽默是如何关联的呢？

sentences.en: So, we find that the emotion, amusement, the judgment, funny, so we have emotion, cognition, and then behavior, laughter, are the three elements that make up a humorous experience.
sentences.zh: 我们发现，情绪（开心）、判断（好笑），也就是说我们有情绪、认知，然后是行为（笑声），这三者构成了幽默体验的三个要素。

sentences.en: They don't all have to be present, but when they are, it tends to be a more intense experience.
sentences.zh: 它们不一定全部存在，但当它们同时出现时，往往会带来更强烈的体验。

sentences.en: Now, laughter is really, I think, the sort of biggest puzzle and the one that I think is most difficult, in part because people are more likely to laugh when others are present,
sentences.zh: 现在，笑声真的是，我认为，最大的谜题，也是我认为最困难的一个，部分原因是因为当有别人在场时，人们更容易笑，

sentences.en: less likely to laugh when no one else is present, right?
sentences.zh: 而当没有其他人在场时，就不太可能笑，对吧？

sentences.en: Because there's nothing to communicate.
sentences.zh: 因为没有什么需要交流的。

sentences.en: Laughter can be faked, right?
sentences.zh: 笑是可以伪装的，对吧？

sentences.en: So, anybody who's had a boss knows that you can fake laughter, right?
sentences.zh: 所以，任何有过老板经历的人都知道，你可以假笑，对吧？

sentences.en: Yep.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And, and laughter can be suppressed.
sentences.zh: 而且，而且笑声是可以被压制的。

sentences.en: That is, someone tells an off-collar joke that you think is funny, but you don't want the world to know that you think that's funny, and so you can stifle, stifle laughter.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，有人讲了一个你觉得好笑的下流笑话，但你不想让全世界知道你觉得这很好笑，所以你可以克制，克制笑声。

sentences.en: And so, but laughter, again, as I said, serves this communication function,
sentences.zh: 所以，但是笑声，就像我刚才说的，具有这种交流的功能，

sentences.en: and we know it does because we see it in species that don't have the ability to articulate ideas in the same way that humans can.
sentences.zh: 我们知道它确实如此，因为我们在那些无法以人类那样的方式清晰表达思想的物种身上也看到了它。

sentences.en: And so, so I, I find that to be a really interesting element to all of this.
sentences.zh: 所以，所以我觉得这是所有这一切中一个非常有趣的元素。

sentences.en: But again, the best, most funny things, you bust a gut, you get that positive, delightful feeling, and you go, Kim, that was hilarious.
sentences.zh: 但话说回来，最好、最搞笑的事情，让你捧腹大笑，带给你那种积极、快乐的感觉，然后你会说，金，太逗了。

sentences.en: That takes me to, to the question about animals and a sense of humor, because we think that what some animals are doing sometimes, and you mentioned rats, that,
sentences.zh: 这就引导我提出了关于动物和幽默感的问题，因为我们认为有些动物有时在做的事情，而且你提到了老鼠，那就是，

sentences.en: that they're laughing.
sentences.zh: 它们在笑。

sentences.en: And I think we have recognized it in some, some apes, some, some of our closer relatives.
sentences.zh: 我想我们已经在某些，某些类人猿，某些，我们较近的亲戚身上意识到了这一点。

sentences.en: But what, what other animals have a sense of humor, and how do we know it?
sentences.zh: 但是，还有哪些动物有幽默感，我们又是如何知道的呢？

sentences.en: Well, you know, this, this question is wide open.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道的，这个，这个问题完全是开放的。

sentences.en: It's, it's not easy to answer.
sentences.zh: 这，这并不容易回答。

sentences.en: The most of the work has been done with, you know, chimps, bonobos, monkeys, apes, and so on.
sentences.zh: 大部分研究都是在，你知道的，黑猩猩、倭黑猩猩、猴子、类人猿等等身上开展的。

sentences.en: The researchers don't call it laughter per se, they call it play panting.
sentences.zh: 研究人员并不称其为严格意义上的笑，他们称之为游戏喘息。

sentences.en: And this is connected, the, the, really, the, the roots of comedy are in play.
sentences.zh: 这与，喜剧的根源，真的，真的在于游戏。

sentences.en: And, and play panting, which is really fascinating, you know, again, is, is this sort of, like, kind of sound.
sentences.zh: 而且，游戏喘息，这真的很迷人，你知道的，也是这种，类似于，某种声音。

sentences.en: And, and what the research shows is that the, the primates that are closest to humans, in genetic, genetically closest to humans, have play panting that,
sentences.zh: 并且，研究显示，与人类最近的灵长类动物，在遗传上最接近人类的灵长类动物，它们的游戏喘息，

sentences.en: that is most akin to the way we laugh.
sentences.zh: 与我们笑的方式最相似。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Right, so we know that they are connected.
sentences.zh: 没错，所以我们知道它们是有联系的。

sentences.en: Now, um, uh, Mark Beckhoff is an expert in animals, and especially an expert in dogs.
sentences.zh: 现在，嗯，呃，马克·贝科夫（Mark Beckhoff）是动物专家，尤其是狗的专家。

sentences.en: And there is emerging work that, that suggests that dogs have a sense of humor, that dogs laugh.
sentences.zh: 而且有越来越多的研究表明，狗有幽默感，狗会笑。

sentences.en: Now, anybody who's a dog owner will say, absolutely, right?
sentences.zh: 任何养狗的人都会说，绝对是的，对吧？

sentences.en: My dog has a sense of humor.
sentences.zh: 我的狗有幽默感。

sentences.en: My dog, quote, unquote, laughs, you know, especially when playing.
sentences.zh: 我的狗，也就是所谓的，会笑，你知道的，特别是在玩耍的时候。

sentences.en: Cat owners, not so much.
sentences.zh: 猫的主人则不那么觉得。

sentences.en: So, it's hard to know.
sentences.zh: 所以，这很难说。

sentences.en: My feeling about this, though, is that any mammal has some, in its repertoire, any mammal that engages in play with its own species, has something akin to humor as a,
sentences.zh: 不过，我对此的感觉是，任何哺乳动物都在其本能中拥有，任何与同类进行游戏的哺乳动物，都拥有一种类似于幽默的东西，作为一种，

sentences.en: an emotional experience.
sentences.zh: 情感体验。

sentences.en: But, again, the work hasn't been done.
sentences.zh: 但是，话说回来，这方面的工作还没有完成。

sentences.en: It, this is, um, this is a projection based upon what's been done and, and the theory I rely on.
sentences.zh: 这，这是，嗯，这是一种基于已有研究以及我所依赖的理论做出的推测。

sentences.en: I think cats laugh, but we can't hear it.
sentences.zh: 我觉得猫会笑，只是我们听不见。

sentences.en: I mean, they certainly laugh at us.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它们绝对在嘲笑我们。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think, yeah, that's true.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想，对，那是真的。

sentences.en: I think they laugh on how they're getting over on the world, yes.
sentences.zh: 我想它们笑是因为它们正在愚弄这个世界，是的。

sentences.en: You teach at a business school, and your most recent book is called Shtick to Business, which is about how lessons from comedy can help people in their work lives.
sentences.zh: 你在商学院教书，你最近的一本书叫做《坚持商业》（Shtick to Business），讲的是喜剧中的教训如何帮助人们的职场生活。

sentences.en: Can you talk about that?
sentences.zh: 你能谈谈这个吗？

sentences.en: And should we, or shouldn't we try to be funny at work?
sentences.zh: 我们到底应不应该在工作中试图表现得有趣呢？

sentences.en: I used to think we should, and now I think only some of us should.
sentences.zh: 我以前认为应该，现在我认为只有我们中的一部分人应该。

sentences.en: So, uh, and I'll make the easy case for why we all should not try to be funnier at work.
sentences.zh: 所以，呃，我会给出一个简单的理由，说明为什么我们并非所有人都在工作时都应该尝试变得有趣。

sentences.en: And it's that guy.
sentences.zh: 那就是那个人。

sentences.en: You know, the guy.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，那家伙。

sentences.en: The guy who thinks he's funny.
sentences.zh: 那个自以为很幽默的家伙。

sentences.en: You know, and so if I tell everybody to go, go forth and be funny at work, we gotta really worry about that guy.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，所以如果我告诉每个人，去吧，去在工作中表现得有趣，我们真得担心那个家伙。

sentences.en: You know what I mean?
sentences.zh: 你知道我的意思吗？

sentences.en: He's like, oh yeah, here's my chance, you know?
sentences.zh: 他会觉得，哦耶，这是我的机会，你知道吗？

sentences.en: And because bad comedy may, you know, at best case bore people, at worst case offend people, the workplace is a place that should be inclusive.
sentences.zh: 因为糟糕的喜剧可能会，你知道的，最好情况下让人感到无聊，最坏情况下冒犯别人，而职场应该是一个具有包容性的地方。

sentences.en: You know, and it should be one where everybody feel welcome and comfortable.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，它应该是一个让每个人都感到受欢迎和舒适的地方。

sentences.en: And so, uh, what I have pivoted my thinking is, is something that everybody should do, which is to think funny.
sentences.zh: 所以，呃，我改变了我的想法，现在认为每个人都应该做到的一点是，进行幽默思考。

sentences.en: And so, as you mentioned at the beginning, I've tried my hand at stand-up.
sentences.zh: 所以，正如你一开始提到的，我也尝试过单口喜剧。

sentences.en: I've taken improv classes.
sentences.zh: 我上过即兴表演课。

sentences.en: I even developed a live comedy show.
sentences.zh: 我甚至开发过一个现场喜剧秀。

sentences.en: And so, I've dipped my toe into the professional world.
sentences.zh: 所以，我曾涉足过这个专业领域。

sentences.en: And what I've realized is, it's incredibly difficult to be successful in that world.
sentences.zh: 而我意识到的是，要在那个领域取得成功是极其困难的。

sentences.en: Yet, those people who are successful in that world, not only are they incredibly creative, sort of innately and intuitively, but there are tips and tricks.
sentences.zh: 然而，那些在那个领域取得成功的人，不仅天生且直觉上就极具创造力，而且还有各种诀窍和技巧。

sentences.en: There are practices and perspectives that they use to make things funnier.
sentences.zh: 他们运用各种实践和视角来使事情变得更有趣。

sentences.en: And it's those practices and perspectives that we can use, not to make comedy, but to make things that are creative or innovative, that can help our lives.
sentences.zh: 正是这些实践和视角，我们可以用来，不是去创作喜剧，而是去创造那些有创意或创新性的事物，从而改善我们的生活。

sentences.en: So, I'll give you a quick example.
sentences.zh: 所以，我给你举个简单的例子。

sentences.en: Comedy 101, the first lesson you learn as a comedian, if you don't already intuitively know it, is what I call reverse it, or the reversal.
sentences.zh: 喜剧入门（Comedy 101），你作为喜剧演员学到的第一课，如果你还没有凭直觉意识到的话，就是我所说的反转，或者说逆转。

sentences.en: And that's to produce an opposing perspective.
sentences.zh: 那就是产生一个相反的视角。

sentences.en: I'll demonstrate it with a joke by Henny Youngman, the king of the one-liners.
sentences.zh: 我用单口喜剧之王亨尼·扬曼（Henny Youngman）的一个笑话来演示一下。

sentences.en: Henny Youngman said, when I read about the dangers of drinking, I gave up.
sentences.zh: 亨尼·扬曼说过，当我读到饮酒的危害时，我戒了。

sentences.en: Kim, what do you think that Henny gave up when he read about the dangers?
sentences.zh: 金，你觉得亨尼读到危害时戒掉了什么？

sentences.en: He gave up reading.
sentences.zh: 他戒了阅读。

sentences.en: He gave up reading.
sentences.zh: 他戒了阅读。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: So, he did the opposite of what you might expect there.
sentences.zh: 所以，他做了你意料之外的相反的事情。

sentences.en: But, you know, that makes that violation benign, because we know Henny likes to drink, you know?
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，这使得这种违背变得无伤大雅，因为我们知道亨尼喜欢喝酒，对吧？

sentences.en: I don't want to give up drinking, so I'll give up reading.
sentences.zh: 我不想戒酒，所以我就戒了阅读。

sentences.en: Well, those reversals, and reversals can be, as I just demonstrated there, the punchline to a joke, but it could also be a premise to a comedy bit.
sentences.zh: 好吧，那些反转，正如我刚才所展示的，反转可以是一个笑话的包袱，但它也可以是一个喜剧段子的前提。

sentences.en: So, the movie Trainwreck, with Amy Schumer, is a reverse rom-com.
sentences.zh: 所以，由艾米·舒默（Amy Schumer）主演的电影《生活残骸》（Trainwreck），就是一部反向的浪漫喜剧。

sentences.en: So, the typical rom-com, boy meets girl, boy loses girl, boy gets girl back.
sentences.zh: 所以，典型的浪漫喜剧是，男孩遇到女孩，男孩失去女孩，男孩把女孩追回来。

sentences.en: In Trainwreck, it's the opposite.
sentences.zh: 在《生活残骸》里，情况正好相反。

sentences.en: Girl meets boy, girl loses boy, girl gets boy back, right?
sentences.zh: 女孩遇到男孩，女孩失去男孩，女孩把男孩追回来，对吧？

sentences.en: Well, you can find the reversal in the real world, and it's often a useful way to break out of very kind of tired, status quo-style thinking.
sentences.zh: 好吧，你可以在现实世界中找到这种反转，这通常是打破那种陈旧的、维持现状式思维的一种有用方法。

sentences.en: I'll give you one quick example of this.
sentences.zh: 我给你举一个这方面的简单例子。

sentences.en: Imagine you're two entrepreneurs based in Brooklyn, and you're looking to take on Apple and Samsung in the smartphone market.
sentences.zh: 想象一下，你是总部设在布鲁克林的两个创业者，你们正准备在智能手机市场上向苹果和三星发起挑战。

sentences.en: How do you outsmart Apple and Samsung?
sentences.zh: 你如何智胜苹果和三星？

sentences.en: Teams of engineers, years and years ahead of you.
sentences.zh: 他们有工程师团队，比你领先好几年。

sentences.en: Well, what these guys did was they reversed it.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这些人所做的是他们进行了反转。

sentences.en: They didn't create a smartphone.
sentences.zh: 他们没有制造智能手机。

sentences.en: They created the dumb phone, right?
sentences.zh: 他们制造了笨蛋手机（dumb phone），对吧？

sentences.en: So, a phone that is made for people who want to be not more connected, but rather less connected.
sentences.zh: 所以，这款手机是为那些不想变得联系更紧密，而是相反，想要减少联系的人准备的。

sentences.en: And so, they've been able to stand out in the marketplace by thinking in reverse.
sentences.zh: 因此，通过逆向思维，他们在市场上脱颖而出。

sentences.en: And so, I invite people to think in reverse, especially when they're stuck on a problem.
sentences.zh: 所以，我邀请人们进行逆向思维，尤其是当他们在某个问题上卡壳的时候。

sentences.en: There's been quite a bit of psychological research into who's funnier, men or women.
sentences.zh: 关于谁更搞笑，男人还是女人，已经有很多心理学研究了。

sentences.en: And, of course, as a woman, I have a point of view here, but I'm going to ask you, what's the answer to that?
sentences.zh: 当然，作为一个女人，我对此有自己的观点，但我还是要问你，这个问题的答案是什么？

sentences.en: I mean, I know there was a recent pretty big meta-analysis that concluded that it's men, but then there's other research that says no.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我知道最近有一个相当大的元分析（meta-analysis）得出结论认为是男性，但也有其他研究说不是。

sentences.en: Is the jury still out?
sentences.zh: 目前还没有定论吗？

sentences.en: I think from a data standpoint, the jury is still out.
sentences.zh: 我认为从数据的角度来看，还没有定论。

sentences.en: There's a lot of work that needs to be done.
sentences.zh: 还有大量的工作要做。

sentences.en: I think it's the wrong question, though.
sentences.zh: 不过，我认为这是一个错误的问题。

sentences.en: I'll be really honeSt.
sentences.zh: 说实话。

sentences.en: I think a lot of the work on gender that compares men and women fails to recognize that men and women are more alike than they are different.
sentences.zh: 我认为许多关于性别的研究，在比较男性和女性时，没有认识到男性和女性的共同点多于不同点。

sentences.en: And so, knowing whether someone is a man or a woman and predicting whether they're going to be funny or not is less important than knowing a whole bunch of other things about them.
sentences.zh: 因此，比起了解一个人是男是女并预测他或她是否搞笑，了解关于他或她的许多其他事情要重要得多。

sentences.en: I'll give you the little work that I've done is, first of all, all of that work is very limited because there are an infinite number of ways to make comedy.
sentences.zh: 我能告诉你的是，我做过的一点点研究表明，首先，所有这些研究都非常有限，因为创作喜剧的方法有无数种。

sentences.en: If you choose one way to make comedy, for example, writing funny captions for cartoons,
sentences.zh: 如果你选择了一种创作喜剧的方法，例如，为漫画编写幽默的标题，

sentences.en: that may tell you that men are better or women are better at making captions for cartoons funny.
sentences.zh: 这可能会告诉你男性或女性更擅长让漫画标题变得搞笑。

sentences.en: But it doesn't explain the vast array that people make things funny.
sentences.zh: 但这并不能解释人们使事物变得搞笑的广阔方式。

sentences.en: Quips, satire, irony, pratfalls, etc.
sentences.zh: 妙语、讽刺、反语、滑稽跌倒等等。

sentences.en: Also, all of that work doesn't do what I think needs to be done is to look at how those jokes fail.
sentences.zh: 此外，所有这些研究都没有做我认为需要做的事情，那就是去看看这些笑话是如何失败的。

sentences.en: And I'll give you an example of a little pilot study I ran.
sentences.zh: 我给你举一个我做过的小型试点研究的例子。

sentences.en: It's not worthy of publication, but I thought it was enlightening.
sentences.zh: 它不值得发表，但我认为它很有启发性。

sentences.en: I did this with my class where I had students doing exactly that, basically making jokes.
sentences.zh: 我让我的班级学生做过这样的事，基本上就是让他们讲笑话。

sentences.en: And then when we measured the funniness of these jokes and we compared men and women, we found that men's jokes tended to be, on average, slightly funnier than women's.
sentences.zh: 然后，当我们衡量这些笑话的搞笑程度并对男性和女性进行比较时，我们发现男性的笑话平均而言比女性的稍微搞笑一点。

sentences.en: So consistent with the existing research.
sentences.zh: 这与现有的研究是一致的。

sentences.en: However, we also measured how offensive the jokes were.
sentences.zh: 然而，我们还衡量了这些笑话的冒犯程度。

sentences.en: And guess what?
sentences.zh: 你猜怎么着？

sentences.en: But the men's jokes were also, when they failed, more likely to be offensive.
sentences.zh: 男性的笑话在失败时，也更有可能具有冒犯性。

sentences.en: And so any good study that compares men and women, which I don't think is that interesting a question, frankly,
sentences.zh: 所以，任何比较男性和女性的优秀研究——坦率地说，我认为这不是一个那么有趣的问题，

sentences.en: because I think there are funny men and there are funny women and there are not funny men and there are not funny women.
sentences.zh: 因为我认为有搞笑的男人，也有搞笑的女人；有不搞笑的男人，也有不搞笑的女人。

sentences.en: But any research has to measure how are you failing, because the failure part of it is as important as part of the success part of it.
sentences.zh: 但是任何研究都必须衡量你是如何失败的，因为失败的部分和成功的部分一样重要。

sentences.en: And so what my hunch is, I can't, you know, I haven't written the papers yet, but my hunch is that depending on how you look at the question, the answer is yes.
sentences.zh: 所以我的直觉是——我不能，你知道的，我还没写出论文，但我的直觉是，取决于你如何看待这个问题，答案是肯定的。

sentences.en: OK.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: You mentioned offensive jokes, and I'm going to venture into the politically incorrect department now and ask, why does it seem that every culture have what we in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 你提到了冒犯性的笑话，现在我要涉足政治不正确领域，问一个问题：为什么每种文化似乎都有我们在美国所说的波兰笑话或笨金发女郎笑话？

sentences.en: call Polish jokes or dumb blonde jokes?
sentences.zh: 当然，我所说的是那些贬低特定群体智力低下的笑话。

sentences.en: And what I'm talking about, of course, is the jokes that denigrate a particular group of people for their supposed lack of intelligence.
sentences.zh: 的确，这似乎是一个普遍现象。

sentences.en: Indeed, that seems to be a universal.
sentences.zh: 雷丁大学（University of Reading）的克里斯蒂·戴维斯（Christy Davies）在这方面做了大量研究。

sentences.en: Christy Davies, who was at the University of Reading, has done a lot of work on this.
sentences.zh: 这确实是一项迷人的工作，主要是定性研究。

sentences.en: It's really fascinating work, qualitative research mostly.
sentences.zh: 本质上，原因在于喜剧可以被用作一种工具。

sentences.en: And essentially, the reason for that is that comedy can be used as a tool.
sentences.zh: 所以它可以被用作娱乐的工具。

sentences.en: So it can be used as a tool to entertain.
sentences.zh: 正如我们讨论幽默抱怨时所说的那样，它可以被用作赢得人们喜爱、吸引眼球的工具。

sentences.en: As we've talked about with Humorous Complaining, it can be used as a tool to get people to like you, to garner attention.
sentences.zh: 但它也可以被用作批评当权者或批评弱者的工具，也就是所谓的向上攻击或向下攻击。

sentences.en: But it also can be used as a tool to critique the powerful or to critique the weak, to punch up or punch down, so to speak.
sentences.zh: 这就是那种通过某种刻板印象、某种既有偏见来取笑某人智力的向下攻击的想法，显然就是向下攻击。

sentences.en: And that's that idea of punching down in terms of making fun of someone's intelligence due to some stereotype, some existing prejudice, is clearly punching down.
sentences.zh: 真的，我认为它主要是出于两个目的设计出来的。

sentences.en: And really, it's just designed, I think, twofold.
sentences.zh: 一是让讲笑话的人感到优越，这也是那种存在了很久的幽默理论的体现。

sentences.en: One is to make the joke teller feel superior, hence that form of theory that has existed for such a long time.
sentences.zh: 然后，它也被用作一种工具，来维持这些差异的存在，继续边缘化、歧视和抱有偏见。

sentences.en: And then it's also just used as a tool to keep those differences in play, to continue to marginalize and to discriminate and to prejudice.
sentences.zh: 所以我相信，最好的喜剧——我不是以研究人员的身份在说，而是作为一个人在说——最好的喜剧是向上攻击的。

sentences.en: And so I believe that the best comedy, I'm not speaking as a researcher, I'm speaking as a human, that the best comedy punches up.
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为最好的喜剧，我不是以研究人员的身份在说，而是作为一个人在说——最好的喜剧是向上攻击的。

sentences.en: It takes on the powerful, and it looks to make the world a better place as a result of that.
sentences.zh: 它挑战强权，并以此让世界变得更美好。

sentences.en: And I think that the best comedy, when it's looking down, is designed to draw people up.
sentences.zh: 我认为最好的喜剧，当它俯视时，其目的是把人们拉起来。

sentences.en: And so I think that good comedians recognize that it is completely inappropriate to make jokes about homosexuals, but it's appropriate to make jokes about homophobes.
sentences.zh: 因此我认为，优秀的喜剧演员意识到，拿同性恋者开玩笑是绝对不合适的，但拿恐同者开玩笑是合适的。

sentences.en: And, you know, and a way to right a wrong, so to speak.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，这可以说是纠正错误的一种方式。

sentences.en: Well, I'm going to put you on the spot, which really probably isn't asking you questions as a researcher, but just as a guy who's interested in humor.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我要让你难堪了，这可能不是以研究人员的身份向你提问，而只是作为一个对幽默感兴趣的人。

sentences.en: What's your favorite joke?
sentences.zh: 你最喜欢什么笑话？

sentences.en: Do you have a favorite comedian, your favorite funny movie?
sentences.zh: 你有最喜欢的喜剧演员或最喜欢的搞笑电影吗？

sentences.en: Well, you know, that's a tough question because it's constantly changing.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道，这是一个很难的问题，因为它一直在变。

sentences.en: We can try this.
sentences.zh: 我们可以试试这个。

sentences.en: This may not work well for a podcast, but you can edit it out if it doesn't work.
sentences.zh: 这可能不太适合播客，但如果效果不好，你可以把它剪掉。

sentences.en: Why don't we do one of my favorite jokes?
sentences.zh: 我们为什么不讲一个我最喜欢的笑话呢？

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 行吧。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Go for it.
sentences.zh: 说吧。

sentences.en: So, Kim, I want you to ask me, what is the secret to good comedy?
sentences.zh: 那么，金，我想让你问我，好的喜剧的秘密是什么？

sentences.en: I know this joke.
sentences.zh: 我知道这个笑话。

sentences.en: What is the secret to good comedy?
sentences.zh: 好的喜剧的秘密是什么？

sentences.en: Timing.
sentences.zh: 时机。

sentences.en: I knew you were going to do that.
sentences.zh: 我就知道你要这么说。

sentences.en: And as you demonstrated, an old joke, and I still laugh at it, right?
sentences.zh: 正如你所展示的，这是一个老笑话，而我仍然会笑，对吧？

sentences.en: I knew it was coming, and it was still funny.
sentences.zh: 我预料到它会来，而且它依然很好笑。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: You know, in terms of favorite comedians, you know, I don't want to pick just one, you know, in part because comedy rewards novelty, you know,
sentences.zh: 你知道，说到最喜欢的喜剧演员，你知道，我不想只选一个，你知道，部分原因是因为喜剧推崇新鲜感，你知道，

sentences.en: so it's easy to fall in love with a new comic.
sentences.zh: 所以很容易爱上一个新的喜剧演员。

sentences.en: But I'm living in Los Angeles right now.
sentences.zh: 但我现在住在洛杉矶。

sentences.en: And last night, I had a wonderful, what felt like pre-pandemic experience.
sentences.zh: 昨晚，我经历了一次美妙的体验，感觉就像疫情前的生活。

sentences.en: I dined outside and had a lovely dinner.
sentences.zh: 我在室外用餐，吃了一顿愉快的晚餐。

sentences.en: And the gentleman at the table to my left, I look up.
sentences.zh: 我左手边桌子上的那位绅士，我抬起头。

sentences.en: He signs the check, walks by me.
sentences.zh: 他签了账单，从我身边走过。

sentences.en: I hear him say something, and I go, I know that voice.
sentences.zh: 我听到他说了一句什么，然后我想，我认得这个声音。

sentences.en: And it was one of my favorite comedians.
sentences.zh: 那是我最喜欢的喜剧演员之一。

sentences.en: I had a Chris Rock sighting last night, which was nearly as delightful as my meal.
sentences.zh: 昨晚我偶遇了克里斯·洛克，这几乎和我的大餐一样令人愉快。

sentences.en: Oh, that's a good story.
sentences.zh: 哦，那是个好故事。

sentences.en: Well, thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: And thank you for joining us today, Dr. McGraw.
sentences.zh: 也感谢你今天加入我们，麦格劳博士。

sentences.en: If I dare say, it's been a real riot talking to you.
sentences.zh: 如果我敢说的话，和你聊天真是一场欢乐的盛宴。

sentences.en: It's been my pleasure.
sentences.zh: 这是我的荣幸。

sentences.en: Thank you, Kim.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，金。

sentences.zh: 你可以在 www.speakingofpsychology.org 或在 Apple、Stitcher 以及其他收听播客的地方找到《心理学说》往期的节目。

sentences.zh: 如果你对未来的播客有什么评论或想法，可以发邮件至 speakingofpsychology@apa.org。

sentences.zh: 那是 speakingofpsychology，所有字母连在一起，@apa.org。

sentences.zh: 《心理学说》由李·韦纳曼制作。

sentences.zh: 我们的音频剪辑师是克里斯·孔达扬。

sentences.en: Thank you for listening.
sentences.zh: 谢谢收听。

sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯，代表美国心理学协会向您问好。
